name: Session-aware serving engine: one residency scheduler for every idle regime (hosted + BYOC)
one_line: A residency scheduler inside vLLM/SGLang (stock KV-connector hooks) plus a session router and control plane that decides per session, from predicted return time, context size and per-tier break-evens, whether KV stays in HBM, moves to RAM/NVMe, or is dropped; sold as a hosted session-addressed endpoint and as BYOC software/optimization engagements for voice and agent platforms and inference providers.

numeric_claims.claim: LMCache eviction: LocalCPUBackend LRU by default; MP EvictionController LRU / IsolatedLRU / noop; no TTL-, time- or idle-window-aware policy documented; Apache-2.0, 11.6k stars; latest release 0.5.4 (Aug 20, 2026)

Tensormesh: $4.5M seed (Oct 2025) + $20M (May 2026) = $24.5M; SaaS bills cached input tokens at $0; Operator 'Coming Soon'; FAQ says SaaS 'in beta'; post-v1 pricing 30% of estimated savings; does not support alternative inference servers; CEO: in-house build takes '20 engineers and three or four months'

Mooncake Store: approximate LRU; default KV lease TTL 10 s; soft-pin TTL default 30 min (max 24 h); hard pins never evicted; SSD offload; DFS tier 'not production-ready'; draft PR #2835 (Jul 10, 2026) TTL-bounded group retention leases, experimental

NVIDIA Dynamo KVBM: G1 GPU / G2 host / G3 disk / G4 object tiers; offload policies pass_all, presence, presence_lfu; per-tier eviction algorithm not detailed and no published performance numbers in the design doc; NVIDIA blog says KVBM exposes cache_control-style TTL retention semantics

llm-d: v0.9.0 (Aug 17, 2026); precise KV-event prefix-cache routing default; OffloadingConnector LRU/ARC tiers; P2P KV pull over NIXL; session affinity; powers GKE Inference Gateway; 219 production Claude Code sessions: median 195K input / 317 output tokens, 96% of requests reuse >=90% of input as verbatim prefix (median 99.6%), inter-turn pauses median 2 s / p99 11.4 min; CPU-DRAM offload at concurrency 32 raised output 13% and cut median TTFT 32%; NVMe tier 'inactive in these measurements'

vLLM OffloadingConnector: built-in eviction policies 'lru' and 'arc', custom policies via cache_policy_module_path, offload_prompt_only default true; RFC #38260 TieringManager open (Mar 26, 2026); KVConnector V1 merged Apr 17, 2025 and still 'experimental and subject to change'; vLLM 0.28.0 (Aug 26, 2026), SGLang 0.5.18 (Aug 21, 2026)

SGLang: RFC #24656 (May 8, 2026) agent-aware KV hints, open and labeled 'inactive'; RFC #27574 (Jun 8, 2026) programmatic KV hints Share/Prefetch/Demote/Pin with bounded TTL, open, first POC pins at Mooncake L3; roadmap #21846 Q3 'Agentic KV Cache Scheduling (session-aware RadixTree, KV cache orchestrator)'; HiCache L1/L2 private per instance, L2 eviction policy undocumented
AIBrix L1 eviction S3FIFO (default), LRU, FIFO

SJTU/Alibaba 'KVCache Cache in the Wild': ideal hit ratios 62% / 54%; 80% of reuses within 10 min (A) or 10 s (B); P99 KV lifespan 97 s; reuse-probability eviction beats LRU/FIFO/LFU by 1.5-3.9% hit rate and up to 41.4% mean response time
Continuum: TTL pinning from reload cost and queueing delay; >8x average job-completion-time improvement on SWE-Bench, BFCL, OpenHands with Llama-3.1 8B/70B, Gemma-3 12B, GLM-4.5 355B
NVIDIA CMX/ICMS flash tier announced for 'second half of 2026'; storage-vendor KV extenders (WEKA, VAST, DDN, Pliops, MinIO) with no pricing found

Proposed thresholds in this brief (not measurements): Metric A ship target >=2x on 3 seeds, kill <1.3x; Metric B kill <15% over LRU, proceed >=25%; predictor hit rate kill <60% / proceed >=80%; NVMe kill >3x modeled restore and break-even >12 h; connector-drift kill >1 engineer-week per release twice; idle ladder {10 s, 2 min, 20 min, 2 h} at C=32

founder_decisions.decision: Hosted endpoint vs BYOC software vs open-source core with paid policy/router/support
founder_decisions.options: (a) Hosted session-addressed endpoint first (dexa FINDINGS direction, dexa_platform + Modal); (b) BYOC connector + policy engine + harness first (voice repo shape); (c) Apache-2.0 connector with a commercial policy engine, router and support
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Depends on the founder's view of PLG vs enterprise motion and on which week-6 design partner converts; the only market data point is Tensormesh selling SaaS in beta while its on-prem Operator is 'coming soon' (05-research-kvcache.md), which is a fact, not a verdict

founder_decisions.decision: Voice-first vs agent-first as the launch regime
founder_decisions.options: (a) Voice: the only measured win (arm D 1.5x, one seed), buyers already priced by concurrency, 26-35B open models on vLLM/SGLang; (b) Agents: 100K+ contexts where measured restore ratios are 10-30x and the SGLang RFCs document the gap, but no policy-vs-LRU measurement exists yet
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: The evidence is asymmetric (voice measured, agents unmeasured) and the answer depends on Metric A (week 2) and Metric B (week 4) results plus the founder's judgment about which buyer is reachable

founder_decisions.decision: Whether the adjacency of Tensormesh/LMCache, NVIDIA Dynamo KVBM, llm-d, Mooncake, and the SGLang RFCs disqualifies or validates the direction
founder_decisions.options: (a) Treat LRU-only eviction and open/inactive RFCs as an unowned layer to occupy now; (b) Treat them as a signal the engines will absorb the policy layer within quarters; (c) Build as an upstream contributor (RFC #27574 implementer) and sell the hosted/BYOC operationalization
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: The brief's hard rule: competitor existence is stated neutrally in section 9; whether it matters is the founder's call, informed by whether the RFCs land and whether Tensormesh's Operator ships

founder_decisions.decision: Model class and GPU class for the proof-of-value
founder_decisions.options: (a) Keep 7B fp16 on L40S (what is measured); (b) Move to buyer-realistic 26-35B models (Gemma 4 26B/31B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) on 80 GB H100/H200; (c) Both, with the H100 sweep as the gate
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Both repos flag larger HBM as the #1 threat (vi-open-larger-hbm-gpu); the H100 sweep is the evidence, and the choice of which hardware to optimize for is a capital and go-to-market decision

founder_decisions.decision: vLLM-only for the six weeks, or vLLM plus SGLang from the start
founder_decisions.options: (a) vLLM 0.28 only (all existing connector code targets vLLM KVConnectorBase_V1); (b) Add SGLang via HiCacheStorage / RFC #27574 hints (LiveKit runs SGLang; the RFC vocabulary matches this brief's hints); (c) SGLang-first as the RFC implementer
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Trades six-week scope against buyer coverage; the repos have zero SGLang connector code and the SGLang path is unmeasured (~30 GPU-h, 10 days estimated)

founder_decisions.decision: Build and measure the NVMe tier now, or after the RAM-tier win is banked
founder_decisions.options: (a) RAM tier only for launch (the only measured tier); (b) NVMe in week 4 (the ~4.9 hr break-even is modeled only); (c) Defer NVMe to storage-vendor partners (WEKA/VAST/DDN on Dynamo/NIXL)
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Depends on whether the founder wants to claim hour-scale idle coverage at launch; the number that decides it does not exist yet

founder_decisions.decision: Whether the open-model voice/agent serving market is large enough to build a company on
founder_decisions.options: Volumes in the files: Vapi 1-5M calls/day, ElevenLabs 10M+ conversations/week, Bland 639M calls to date; LLM share of a voice minute ranges from under 5% (Inworld, self-hosted Gemma) to ~30% (smallest.ai) to 'usually the largest line' (Deepgram); open-weight models a majority of OpenRouter tokens by mid-2026
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: Market-size judgments are explicitly reserved for the founder per the hard rules; the brief states the volumes and cost shares neutrally

founder_decisions.decision: Whether the return-time hint protocol is an open spec or proprietary
founder_decisions.options: (a) Publish it and drive SGLang RFC #27574 / vLLM adoption so orchestrators (LiveKit, Pipecat, OpenHands, Claude Code harnesses) emit hints natively; (b) Keep it proprietary as the moat; (c) Open the wire format, keep the policy engine closed
founder_decisions.why_not_ours_to_make: A strategic openness decision; the evidence that informs it is whether hint adoption by orchestrators is the bottleneck (unmeasured) and whether the RFCs land without the company
